hook: India's first bullet train seats *557*, built in Bengaluru
hook_b: 249 km/h, Wi-Fi, 3×2 seats: meet India's bullet train *B28*
tldr: B28, for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad line, tests at 280 km/h, runs at 249 km/h and seats about 557.

beats.what: Details of B28, the indigenous trainset for the Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet corridor, are out.
beats.why: India is building its own high-speed train at BEML instead of only importing one.
beats.care: Seven of eight coaches are standard class. Fares and launch date are not announced.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: B28 is about 202 m long: 4 motor cars and 4 trailer cars. Seven standard coaches have 3×2 seats; one executive coach has 2×2. Space for 2 wheelchair users, level boarding, Braille signs. LCD info in English, Hindi and regional languages, Wi-Fi infotainment with preloaded content, charging points. Runs on 25 kV AC with regenerative braking. Launch date and fares were not in the report.

cards.title: ♿ Built in
cards.body: Floor level with the platform, retractable footsteps, wheelchair-wide doors, accessible seats and toilet.

cards.q: What matters most in a bullet train for you?
Where is the B28 bullet train being built?
cards.why: It is being made indigenously at BEML's Aditya Plant in Bengaluru.

insight: BEML is building the 8-coach B28 at its Aditya Plant in Bengaluru; two can couple into 16 coaches.
watch: Trial-run dates and fares for Mumbai–Ahmedabad.
